people.name: Pol Pot
people.description: Cambodian dictator whose Khmer Rouge regime killed approximately 1.5-2 million people (25% of the population) through execution, forced labor, and starvation in pursuit of an agrarian utopia.

people.name: Leopold II of Belgium
people.description: Personally owned the Congo Free State and exploited it for rubber, causing an estimated 10 million deaths through forced labor, mutilation, and starvation.

people.name: Adolf Hitler
people.description: Nazi Germany's dictator who orchestrated the Holocaust, systematically murdering six million Jews and millions of others. Started World War II, causing approximately 70-85 million deaths.

people.name: Joseph Stalin
people.description: Soviet dictator whose policies caused the deaths of millions through forced collectivization, political purges, and the Gulag system. His Great Terror eliminated perceived enemies through show trials and mass executions.

people.name: Mao Zedong
people.description: Chinese Communist leader whose Great Leap Forward caused a famine killing 15-55 million people. The Cultural Revolution destroyed countless lives and cultural heritage.

people.name: Andrew Jackson
people.description: U.S. President who signed the Indian Removal Act, forcing the relocation of Native Americans in the Trail of Tears, causing thousands of deaths.

people.name: Francisco Franco
people.description: Ruled Spain through authoritarian control after a civil war, repressing political opponents for decades through violent repression and cultural suppression.

people.name: Henry Morton Stanley
people.description: Explorer who helped establish Leopold II's brutal Congo regime by making treaties with local leaders who didn't understand they were signing away sovereignty.

people.name: Bull Connor
people.description: Birmingham, Alabama's Commissioner of Public Safety who ordered police dogs and fire hoses used against civil rights protesters, including children.

people.name: Augusto Pinochet
people.description: Chilean dictator who seized power in a coup and oversaw the torture, disappearance, and murder of thousands of political opponents.

people.name: Robert Mugabe
people.description: Zimbabwe's leader who initially brought independence but later oversaw political violence, rigged elections, and economic policies that caused hyperinflation and widespread poverty.

people.name: Benito Mussolini
people.description: Established a fascist dictatorship in Italy, suppressed dissent, and pursued imperial aggression. Seen as a cautionary example of how nationalism and authoritarianism corrode institutions.

people.name: Christopher Columbus
people.description: Italian explorer whose voyages initiated European colonization of the Americas, leading to the exploitation, enslavement, and decimation of indigenous populations through disease and violence.

people.name: Genghis Khan
people.description: Mongol conqueror who built the largest empire in history through mass invasions, resulting in the deaths of up to 40 million people and widespread destruction.

people.name: Josef Mengele
people.description: SS physician at Auschwitz who performed deadly human experiments on prisoners without consent. Reviled as the 'Angel of Death'.

people.name: Cecil Rhodes
people.description: British imperialist whose policies dispossessed Africans of land and rights, laying the foundations for apartheid.

people.name: Roger Taney
people.description: Chief Justice who authored the Dred Scott decision, ruling Black Americans couldn't be citizens and Congress couldn't ban slavery.

people.name: Hernan Cortes
people.description: Spanish conquistador whose campaigns caused the Aztec Empire's fall through warfare, disease, and brutal colonial rule.

people.name: King John I of England
people.description: Tyrannical monarch whose abuses provoked the Magna Carta, though the document initially only protected nobility.

people.name: The Robber Barons
people.description: Industrial magnates like Rockefeller, Carnegie, and Morgan who built monopolies through worker exploitation and political corruption in the late 19th century.
